I took it down from a 5 for two reasons. Second, the date for speedwork is loose ("around the second week of November") and isn't tied to her actual race date or her 3:45 goal. Going back to the 40-mile range is also left open, with no next step past this week. Still a strong, safe reply.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 42, 46, 34, 41 mi
This week: 12 mi over 3 runs.
Body: "Legs came back by Thursday. Blister healed."
Feeling: "Itching to train again."
Asks: "I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Recovery is going well, so step up gently to about 22 miles of all-easy running this week, not 40 with speedwork. …
Answers: (1) Not yet, on both counts. A classic guide after a marathon is about one easy day per race mile before hard training, which puts real speedwork around the second week of November for you. (2) For the Thanksgiving 10K, it is possible but I would not call it a goal race. If you want to jog it as a hard training day, fine.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to protect the rebuild.
Tue: easy, 4 mi, conversational, heart rate under 140. First run of the week, keep it…
Wed: easy, 5 mi, same easy effort, flat route if you can. Adds a touch of volume without…
Thu: easy, 3 mi, very relaxed shakeout. Keeps the legs ticking between the midweek run…
Fri: rest. Normal rest day, treat it as real rest.
Sat: easy, 3 mi, conversational. Primes the legs for Sunday without draining them.
Sun: easy, 7 mi, all easy, no pace work. Rebuilds the long-run habit at a safe size.
